thread:
alex: FYI support ticket #4321 — ACME reporting sudden 5xx/504s for hosted inference endpoints since ~12:05 PST. p95 latency shot up to >12s, a bunch of timeouts. customer says they see a lot of `504 gateway_timeout` + `502` errors.

maya: Got logs from the gateway for that tenant. Queue depth spiked and batchers went into backlog. Looks like continuous batching queues never drained.

alex: Customer pasted a snippet of their client behavior — they rotate auth tokens every 60s and several requests got 401s, client retries immediately with exponential jitter but aggressive (0,100,200ms). Could be retry storm.

tim: I'm seeing the same on the runtime metrics. Request queue depth for region us-west-2 jumped from ~150 to ~1400 at 12:04. Continuous batching backlog metric `batcher.pending_requests` stayed >1000 for ~6m.

jordan: Can you paste the gateway logs? specifically early-reject/queue-reject lines and the batcher stack traces.

maya: Pasting relevant log extracts (sanitized):

```
2026-03-15T12:04:02Z gateway INFO request accepted tenant=acme id=... route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T12:04:03Z gateway WARN auth failed status=401 tenant=acme token_id=rot-123
2026-03-15T12:04:03Z client-retry INFO retrying req=... backoff=0ms
2026-03-15T12:04:04Z runtime WARN batcher pending=1208 model=rw-7b seq=512
2026-03-15T12:04:07Z gateway ERROR queue_depth_exceeded tenant=acme depth=1402 reject=true
2026-03-15T12:04:07Z runtime ERROR tail_timeout req=... reason=kv-cache-starve
```

maya: Also saw lots of `client-retry` entries immediately after 401s. Looks like token rotation caused bursts of retries that filled the queue and the runtime couldn't keep up — tail-latency timeouts followed.

alex: Customer says billing automation started rotating tokens after a failed payment status check. So billing->auth rotation -> client retries -> queue spike. Lovely.

kira: What's our immediate mitigation? Can we per-tenant throttle / disable continuous batching for that tenant quickly?

tim: We can toggle per-tenant flags. Quick options: 1) enable early-reject at 500 depth (currently 2000 global), 2) lower continuous-batching max_batch_size for that tenant, 3) add temporary per-tenant QPS cap, 4) instruct customer to back off retries.

jordan: I recommend (3) + (2) as fastest. Early-reject could cause a flood of 429s which might cascade, but controlled QPS cap will slow incoming rate. Also we should disable prefix caching for tenant to free KV resources.

maya: I'll run the per-tenant throttle. Command: `infractl tenants update acme --rate-limit=10rps --disable-continuous-batching=true` (dry-run first then apply).

tim: I'll prepare a small hotfix to add a `retry-window` heuristic on the gateway so repeated auth-failure + retries get a short client-side ban (like 5s) to avoid immediate bursts. But that's not hotfixable immediately — needs a small rollout.

alex: Meanwhile I'm on the support thread telling ACME to pause token rotation and reduce client retry aggressiveness. Asking for a config they can change now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by tim — hotfix/tenant-throttle (sha: a1b2c3) to infra-config.

jordan: After applying `--rate-limit=10rps` and disabling continuous batching for acme, queue depth dropped from 1400 -> 180 within 90s. p95 dropped from 12s -> 420ms.

maya: Confirmed on metrics: `batcher.pending_requests{tenant=acme}` trending down. No new 504s post-mitigation.

alex: Customer says errors subsided at ~12:09 and most requests succeeded. They're going to revert token rotation while we investigate root cause.

kira: For postmortem we should capture: why did continuous batching not shed load earlier? It should picked up heavy tail and shrink batch size. Maybe the batcher backpressure thresholds are too lenient for per-tenant bursts.

jordan: Agree. Action items I propose: 1) add per-tenant backpressure signals into router so we can early-route or reject before runtime, 2) add a retry-storm detector in gateway that looks for auth 401 -> immediate retries window, 3) add customer-facing best-practice doc about token rotation and retry jittering.

tim: I'll open an RFC for per-tenant backpressure and priority queueing. Also will create a small runtime patch to make continuous batching drop to single-inflight per-tenant when pending > 200.

maya: Notes on repro steps for eng:
- reproduce: run auth-rotation-sim.py (attached) which rotates tokens every 60s and retries on 401 with jitter [0,100,200ms]
- load: 50rps baseline steady, rotation bump to ~1200 concurrent over 30s
- expected: early-reject/429s if throttled, not 504s

alex: Customer follow-up: they accepted guidance to add exponential backoff with randomized base jitter and will test. They also asked for a root-cause writeup.

kira: I'll draft a short RCA and add recommended config snippets. Also will coordinate with docs to publish the retry/storm best-practices page.

jordan: Closing notes: immediate mitigation worked; no infra-wide incident, isolated to tenant. Action items assigned: tim (per-tenant backpressure RFC), jordan (runtime threshold patch), kira (RCA + docs), maya (monitoring alerts for retry storms).

alex: Thanks all. Marking as resolved for now; reopening if ACME sees any regression. :white_check_mark:
